paper.title: Online Influence Maximization with Semi-Bandit Feedback under Corruptions

settings.name_in_paper: Online influence maximization under corruption (IC model, edge semi-bandit feedback, linear generalization of activation probabilities)
unmapped: Independent cascade diffusion on a known directed graph; base arms are edges with activation probability p(e)=x_e^T theta (known edge features, unknown theta)
Corruption: each corrupted node u shifts activation probabilities of all its out-edges by c_{u,t}; C = max_u sum_t |c_{u,t}| (per-node budget, maximum over nodes)
Reward is expected influence spread f(S), satisfying monotonicity and 1-norm bounded smoothness with constant B
Learner knows the graph topology (hence E^* and E^c) and has access to an (alpha,gamma)-approximation oracle for offline IM
settings.definition_quote: For a normal user, the activation probability $p(e)$ of any out-edge $e$ can always be well-approximated as $p(e) = \boldsymbol{x}_{e}^T\boldsymbol{\theta}$, whereas for any corrupted user $u \in \mathcal{V}$, the activation probability of its out-edge $e$ at $t$ is given by $p_t(e) = \boldsymbol{x}_{e}^T\boldsymbol{\theta} + c_{u,t}$. ... $R^{\alpha \gamma}(T) = T \cdot f_{D,\boldsymbol{P}}(\mathcal{S}^{opt}) - \frac{1}{\alpha \gamma}\mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T f_{D,\boldsymbol{P}}(\mathcal{S}_t)]$

symbols.B_smooth: 1-norm bounded smoothness constant of the expected spread (B = largest number of nodes reachable from any node)
symbols.E_star: number of edges in the first min{l,K_seed} (largest) connected subgraphs, E^* <= m_edges
symbols.E_c: sum over the first min{l,K_seed} subgraphs of the maximum number of descendant edges of a node, E^c <= E^*
symbols.n_nodes: number of users (nodes) in the graph

conditions: Activation probabilities follow Assumption 3 (linear in known edge features plus per-node corruption c_{u,t})
Independent cascade diffusion model with edge semi-bandit feedback
tuning: beta >= sigma^{-2} sqrt(d log(1+E^*T/d) + 2 log(nT)) + sigma^{-2} lambda E^c C + Theta

source.label: the:rgt
source.quote: Assume that the activation probability of users satisfy Assumption~\ref{assump:clb-p}. Besides, \textsc{ORACLE} is an $(\alpha,\gamma)$-approximation algorithm. Let $\Theta$ be the known upper bound on $\norm{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$, $C \geq 0$ is the corruption budget, $\lambda= \frac{\sqrt{d}}{CE^c}$. For any $\sigma > 0$ and any $x_e \in \mathbb{R}^d$, ... if $\beta$ satisfies ... the $\alpha \gamma$-scaled regret is upper bounded as $R^{\alpha \gamma}(T) \leq O(dBE^*\sqrt{T}\log(nT) + BE^*E^cCd\log(nT))$.

results.notes: The regret is alpha*gamma-scaled regret in expectation against the uncorrupted spread f_{D,P}, so it is recorded as alpha_regret. The bound depends on graph topology (E^*, E^c), so 'worst_case' here means not gap-dependent. Remark 7 gives the topology-free version O(dmB sqrt(T) log(nT) + B m^2 C d log(nT)) using E^c, E^* <= m. Noise: activations are Bernoulli but the proof only uses bounded zero-mean noise. Compute depends on the oracle, so it is recorded as not_stated.
